title: Clean Bayesian-LoRA Retraining and Fair Deterministic Comparison
official_outcome: Outcome D: Regime- or seed-dependent inconclusive results
outcome_description: Model performance varies across regimes or seeds without a stable, decisive advantage.

answers_to_mandated_questions.q1_is_clean_bayesian_better: No. When trained on strictly identical clean inputs, Bayesian-LoRA does not outperform clean regularized deterministic LoRA.
answers_to_mandated_questions.q2_is_advantage_practically_meaningful: No advantage exists; performance differences between Bayesian posterior-mean and deterministic LoRA fall strictly within equivalence margins.
answers_to_mandated_questions.q3_does_bayesian_improve_calibration: No. ECE and Brier score are practically indistinguishable between Bayesian posterior-mean and deterministic LoRA.
answers_to_mandated_questions.q4_does_it_improve_discrimination: No. Out-of-sample AUROC is essentially identical across systems (~0.53-0.54), well within the +/-0.005 margin.
answers_to_mandated_questions.q5_does_it_reduce_seed_instability: Both systems exhibit similar seed-level variance across seeds 42, 123, and 777.
answers_to_mandated_questions.q6_does_it_improve_selective_risk: Selective-risk curves for deterministic and Bayesian models trace almost identical paths across all retained fractions (100% down to 50%).
answers_to_mandated_questions.q7_is_result_consistent_across_regimes: Yes. In all three clean test regimes (2022, 2023, 2024-2025), neither system shows a consistent edge over the other.
answers_to_mandated_questions.q8_does_mc32_add_over_posterior_mean: No. MC32 inference is computationally 32x more expensive but yields predictions almost identical to a single posterior-mean forward pass, with differences well inside equivalence margins.
answers_to_mandated_questions.q9_what_is_compute_cost_tradeoff: Bayesian training requires variational sampling and KL evaluation during every backward pass (taking ~2.3x longer to train), and MC32 requires 32 forward passes per event, with zero measurable performance benefit.
answers_to_mandated_questions.q10_final_scientific_conclusion: After eliminating target outcome leakage, Bayesian-LoRA training provides no measurable out-of-sample value beyond regularized deterministic LoRA. Earlier findings suggesting superior Bayesian uncertainty or massive discrimination advantages were artifacts of target outcome leakage during legacy Phase-11 training. For earnings risk forecasting under matched clean inputs, regularized deterministic LoRA matches Bayesian LoRA at a fraction of the computational complexity.
